findings.summary: subtotal loops range(len(items)-1), skipping the last line item.
findings.failure_scenario: For items=[{"price":100,"qty":1},{"price":200,"qty":1}], the loop runs i in range(1) so it only sums the first item, returning 100 instead of 300. Every invoice undercounts by omitting its final line item; a single-item invoice returns 0.

findings.summary: mean_line_value divides by len(items) with no empty-list guard, raising ZeroDivisionError.
findings.failure_scenario: mean_line_value([]) computes subtotal([]) // 0, raising ZeroDivisionError instead of returning 0 or handling empty input. Additionally the mean is wrong because subtotal itself omits the last item.

findings.summary: allocate_tax divides by sum(weights) with no zero guard, raising ZeroDivisionError.
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(100, [0,0]) or allocate_tax(100, []) has total==0, so tax_cents*w/total raises ZeroDivisionError.

findings.summary: allocate_tax rounds each share independently, so the allocated cents may not sum to tax_cents.
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(10, [1,1,1]) yields [round(3.33), round(3.33), round(3.33)] = [3,3,3] summing to 9, losing a cent; other splits can over-allocate. Integer-cent tax must sum exactly to tax_cents (e.g. by giving the remainder to one item).

findings.summary: late_fee returns a negative fee for negative days_late instead of clamping to zero.
findings.failure_scenario: late_fee(-3) returns -1500, i.e. a credit, when a not-yet-overdue order should incur no fee (result 0).

findings.summary: subtotal iterates range(len(items)-1), skipping the last line item so the total is always short by the final item.
findings.failure_scenario: subtotal([{"price":100,"qty":1},{"price":200,"qty":1}]) returns 100 instead of 300 because index 1 (the last item) is never visited; a single-item invoice returns 0.

findings.summary: mean_line_value divides by len(items) with no guard, raising ZeroDivisionError on an empty list, and inherits subtotal's off-by-one under-count.
findings.failure_scenario: mean_line_value([]) raises ZeroDivisionError; and mean_line_value([{"price":100,"qty":1}]) returns 0//1=0 instead of 100 because subtotal drops the last item.

findings.summary: allocate_tax rounds each share independently, so the allocations do not necessarily sum to tax_cents (money is lost or created).
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(10, [1,1,1]) gives round(3.33..) for each = [3,3,3] summing to 9, not 10; the missing cent is never distributed. For losing more, larger sets diverge further from tax_cents.

findings.summary: allocate_tax divides by total=sum(weights) with no guard, raising ZeroDivisionError when weights are empty or all zero.
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(100, []) or allocate_tax(100, [0,0]) raises ZeroDivisionError instead of returning an empty/zero allocation.

findings.summary: late_fee does not clamp negative days_late, returning a negative (credit) fee for orders paid early.
findings.failure_scenario: late_fee(-3) returns -1500, applying a negative late fee instead of 0 for an order that is not overdue.

findings.summary: subtotal iterates range(len(items)-1), dropping the last line item from the sum.
findings.failure_scenario: For items=[{"price":100,"qty":1},{"price":200,"qty":1}], the loop runs i in range(1) only, so it returns 100 instead of 300. Any single-item list returns 0.

findings.summary: mean_line_value raises ZeroDivisionError on empty items and inherits subtotal's missing-last-item error.
findings.failure_scenario: mean_line_value([]) does 0 // 0 -> ZeroDivisionError. For non-empty lists, subtotal already omits the last item so the numerator is too small, yielding a wrong average.

findings.summary: allocate_tax divides by sum(weights), raising ZeroDivisionError when all weights are zero (or list is empty).
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(100, [0, 0]) computes total=0 and evaluates 100*0/0 -> ZeroDivisionError; allocate_tax(100, []) also gives total=0 (returns [] but division not reached).

findings.summary: allocate_tax rounds each share independently, so the allocated cents need not sum to tax_cents.
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(10, [1,1,1]) yields [round(3.33),round(3.33),round(3.33)]=[3,3,3]=9, losing a cent; the total tax distributed does not equal the input tax_cents.

findings.summary: late_fee returns a negative fee for negative days_late instead of clamping to zero.
findings.failure_scenario: late_fee(-3) returns -1500, a negative "late fee" for an order that is not overdue, rather than 0.

findings.summary: can_refund relies on and/or precedence which allows a shipped, cancelled order to be refundable and depends on all three keys existing.
findings.failure_scenario: Due to precedence it evaluates (paid and not shipped) or cancelled; an order {"paid":False,"shipped":True,"cancelled":True} returns True, and any order missing e.g. the "cancelled" key raises KeyError.

findings.summary: subtotal() iterates range(len(items)-1), skipping the last line item and undercounting the total.
findings.failure_scenario: With items=[{"price":100,"qty":1},{"price":200,"qty":1}], the loop runs i in range(1)=[0], adding only 100 and returning 100 instead of 300. A single-item invoice returns 0.

findings.summary: mean_line_value() divides by len(items) with no guard, raising ZeroDivisionError on empty input.
findings.failure_scenario: mean_line_value([]) computes subtotal([])//len([]) = 0//0, raising ZeroDivisionError instead of returning 0 or handling empty invoices.

findings.summary: mean_line_value() divides the buggy subtotal (missing last item) by the full item count, producing a wrong average.
findings.failure_scenario: With items=[{"price":100,"qty":1},{"price":300,"qty":1}], subtotal returns 100 (last item skipped) and dividing by 2 gives 50, whereas the true average is 200.

findings.summary: allocate_tax() divides by sum(weights) with no guard, raising ZeroDivisionError when weights is empty or all zeros.
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(100, []) or allocate_tax(100, [0,0]) makes total=0, so tax_cents*w/total raises ZeroDivisionError.

findings.summary: allocate_tax() rounds each share independently, so the allocated amounts need not sum to tax_cents (money is lost or created).
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(100, [1,1,1]) yields [round(33.33)]*3 = [33,33,33] summing to 99, not 100; the missing cent is never allocated, so the tax split doesn't reconcile.

findings.summary: can_refund() returns True for any cancelled order regardless of payment status, allowing refunds of never-paid orders.
findings.failure_scenario: order={"paid":False,"shipped":True,"cancelled":True} returns True because the 'or cancelled' clause short-circuits the paid/shipped check, permitting a refund on an unpaid order.

findings.summary: late_fee() does not clamp negative days_late, returning a negative fee for orders not yet overdue.
findings.failure_scenario: late_fee(-3) returns -1500 instead of 0, producing a negative (credit) late fee for an order paid early.

findings.summary: median does not average the two middle values for even-length input, contradicting its docstring.
findings.failure_scenario: median([1, 2, 3, 4]) returns s[2] = 3 instead of the documented (2+3)/2 = 2.5. Any even-length list returns the upper-middle element rather than the mean of the two middle values.

findings.summary: percentile indexes out of range for p=100 (and near the top), causing IndexError.
findings.failure_scenario: percentile([1,2,3,4], 100) computes int(4*100/100) = 4 and evaluates s[4] on a length-4 list, raising IndexError. The nearest-rank index should be clamped or use ceil(p/100*n)-1.

findings.summary: moving_average uses range(len(xs)-k) which drops the final window, producing one fewer result than expected.
findings.failure_scenario: moving_average([1,2,3,4], 2) yields windows for i in 0,1 -> [1.5, 2.5], missing the last window [3,4]->3.5. Correct count is len(xs)-k+1, so range should be range(len(xs)-k+1). For k==len(xs) it returns [] instead of the single full-window average.

findings.summary: mean raises ZeroDivisionError on empty input instead of handling it gracefully.
findings.failure_scenario: mean([]) computes sum([])/len([]) = 0/0 and raises ZeroDivisionError. Similarly median([]), sample_range([]), and percentile([], p) raise on empty input; no guard is provided.

findings.summary: subtotal loops range(len(items)-1), dropping the last line item from the sum.
findings.failure_scenario: Given items=[{"price":100,"qty":1},{"price":200,"qty":1}], the loop iterates i in range(1) only, returning 100 instead of 300. Every invoice undercounts by its last line item; a single-item invoice returns 0.

findings.summary: mean_line_value divides by len(items) with no empty-list guard, raising ZeroDivisionError.
findings.failure_scenario: mean_line_value([]) computes subtotal([])//0 and raises ZeroDivisionError instead of returning 0 or handling empty input. (Also inherits subtotal's off-by-one, so non-empty results are wrong.)

findings.summary: allocate_tax divides by total=sum(weights) with no guard for zero/empty weights.
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(100, []) or allocate_tax(100, [0,0]) makes total=0 and each element computes tax_cents*w/0, raising ZeroDivisionError.

findings.summary: allocate_tax's per-item round() can make the allocated cents not sum to tax_cents.
findings.failure_scenario: allocate_tax(10, [1,1,1]) yields [round(3.33),round(3.33),round(3.33)] = [3,3,3] summing to 9, not 10; the missing cent is never distributed, so allocated tax does not reconcile with the invoice total.

findings.summary: late_fee returns a negative fee for negative days_late (not-yet-overdue orders).
findings.failure_scenario: late_fee(-3) returns -1500, applying a negative late fee (credit) instead of clamping to 0 for orders that are not overdue.

findings.summary: median does not average the two middle values for even-length input as its docstring promises.
findings.failure_scenario: median([1, 2, 3, 4]) returns s[4//2] = s[2] = 3, but the documented/correct result is (2+3)/2 = 2.5. For any even-length list the function returns the upper-middle element instead of the mean of the two middle elements.

findings.summary: moving_average uses range(len(xs) - k), dropping the last valid window (off-by-one).
findings.failure_scenario: moving_average([1,2,3,4], 2) iterates i in range(2) = 0,1, producing [1.5, 2.5] and omitting the final window [3,4]->3.5. There are len(xs)-k+1 = 3 windows; the correct range is range(len(xs)-k+1). Also when k == len(xs) the result is [] instead of one full-window average.

findings.summary: percentile indexes out of range for p=100 and mis-ranks other percentiles.
findings.failure_scenario: percentile([1,2,3,4], 100) computes int(4*100/100) = 4 and evaluates s[4], raising IndexError since valid indices are 0..3. For nearest-rank the index should be ceil(p/100*n)-1 (clamped). Additionally p=0 gives index 0 which is fine, but intermediate values are off: percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) yields s[2]=3 rather than the 2nd-of-4 nearest-rank value.

findings.summary: mean raises ZeroDivisionError on an empty list instead of handling it.
findings.failure_scenario: mean([]) computes sum([])/len([]) = 0/0, raising ZeroDivisionError. Similarly median([]), sample_range([]) (max of empty raises ValueError), and percentile([], p) fail on empty input with no graceful handling.

findings.summary: median does not average the two middle values for even-length inputs, contradicting its docstring.
findings.failure_scenario: median([1, 2, 3, 4]) returns s[2] = 3 instead of the documented (2+3)/2 = 2.5. For any even-length list the result is wrong (biased to the upper-middle element).

findings.summary: percentile raises IndexError for p=100 and generally computes the wrong nearest-rank index.
findings.failure_scenario: percentile([1,2,3,4], 100) computes index int(4*100/100)=4, then s[4] raises IndexError (valid indices 0..3). Even for interior values the nearest-rank formula is off (e.g. p=50 on 4 elements yields index 2, not the expected rank).

findings.summary: moving_average uses range(len(xs)-k), dropping the final valid window (off-by-one).
findings.failure_scenario: moving_average([1,2,3,4], 2) iterates i in range(2) = 0,1, producing 2 averages [1.5, 2.5] but the correct output has 3 windows (len-k+1): [1.5, 2.5, 3.5]. The last window is always omitted. Additionally when k==len(xs) it returns [] instead of one average.

findings.summary: mean divides by zero on empty input, raising ZeroDivisionError.
findings.failure_scenario: mean([]) computes sum([])/len([]) = 0/0 and raises ZeroDivisionError instead of handling the empty case; similar unguarded empty-input failures affect median/sample_range/percentile.

findings.summary: median() does not average the two middle values for even-length input, contradicting its documented behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: median([1, 2, 3, 4]) returns s[2] == 3 instead of the documented (2+3)/2 == 2.5. For any even-length list it returns the upper-middle element rather than the average of the two middle values.

findings.summary: percentile() with p=100 computes index len(s) which is out of range, raising IndexError.
findings.failure_scenario: percentile([1, 2, 3], 100) computes int(3 * 100 / 100) == 3 and evaluates s[3], raising IndexError even though p=100 is documented as valid. Nearest-rank should clamp/round so the top percentile maps to the last element.

findings.summary: moving_average() uses range(len(xs)-k), dropping the final valid window (off-by-one).
findings.failure_scenario: moving_average([1,2,3,4], 2) iterates i in range(2) → i=0,1, producing 2 averages [1.5, 2.5] and omitting the last window [3,4]→3.5. There are len(xs)-k+1 == 3 windows; the loop should be range(len(xs)-k+1).

findings.summary: moving_average() divides by k with no guard, causing ZeroDivisionError when k=0.
findings.failure_scenario: moving_average([1,2,3], 0) evaluates sum(xs[i:i])/0 → ZeroDivisionError. Also for k > len(xs) it silently returns an empty list rather than signaling an error.

findings.summary: median() does not average the two middle values for even-length input, contradicting its docstring.
findings.failure_scenario: median([1, 2, 3, 4]) returns s[2]=3 instead of the documented average of the two middle values (2+3)/2=2.5.

findings.summary: percentile() indexes out of range when p=100 (or high p), causing IndexError.
findings.failure_scenario: percentile([1,2,3,4], 100) computes int(4*100/100)=4 and evaluates s[4], which raises IndexError since valid indices are 0..3.

findings.summary: moving_average() uses range(len(xs)-k), dropping the final valid window (off-by-one).
findings.failure_scenario: moving_average([1,2,3,4], 2) returns [1.5, 2.5] (indices 0,1) but omits the window [3,4]=3.5; should iterate range(len(xs)-k+1).

findings.summary: mean() (and median/sample_range/percentile) raise on empty input with no guard.
findings.failure_scenario: mean([]) raises ZeroDivisionError; sample_range([]) and median([]) raise on max/empty index — no empty-list handling is provided.
